correctness.rationale: Lucas digit comparison is equivalent to nonzero coefficients modulo p. For every multiplier m invertible and not 1 mod p and every carry c, the affine digit map d -> (m d+c) mod p has exactly (p+1)/2 digits with output >= input. The proof counts both increments and wrap-around decrements under c -> c+1, then averages across c. State-independent branching proves every finite-depth and suffix count without a terminal carry restriction (higher n digits are zero). Uniform cylinder masses give the stated Hausdorff and box dimensions and Ahlfors regularity. The verifier independently exercised 14130 exact finite assertions; none is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural arithmetic invariant counts nonzero proportional-binomial coefficients along entire rays through Pascal triangle, not arbitrary slices. The exact universality over all odd primes and all multipliers in two-thirds of residue classes is unexpected from Lucas digit arithmetic; its underpinning is a nontrivial state-independent affine excedance lemma. It yields uniform counts after every prescribed index suffix, a sharp regular p-adic fractal with exact cylinder masses, and explicit exceptional-slope contrast. This is mathematically more informative than mere sparseness or a single small-modulus numerical census.
